issue: Must a district court consider the 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) sentencing factors when deciding whether to reduce a sentence under § 404 of the First Step Act, or may it decline to do so?

sides.position: District courts must consider all applicable § 3553(a) factors when resolving a § 404 sentence-reduction motion.
cases: United States v. Easter, 975 F.3d 318 (3d Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Consideration of the § 3553(a) factors is discretionary; a court may consider them but is not required to (the Eighth Circuit says 'may, but need not'; the Seventh Circuit describes using them as permissible).
cases: United States v. Moore, 963 F.3d 725 (8th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Williams, 943 F.3d 841 (8th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Shaw, 957 F.3d 734 (7th Cir. 2020)

this_court: must consider all applicable § 3553(a) factors (the court expressly declines to follow the Eighth Circuit's reading in Moore)
quote: We decline to follow our sister circuits for four reasons.
cite: United States v. Jamel Easter, 975 F.3d 318 (3rd Cir. 2020)
